title: A prospective, multicenter, non-interventional study on the prophylaxis of recurrent urinary tract infections with Cystohipp® (methenamine hippurate) to generate real-world evidence in routine urological care in Germany
summary: Cystohipp® was developed for the prophylaxis of uncomplicated lower urinary tract infections (UTIs). Its active ingredient, methenamine, has been known for many years, is effective against a broad range of bacterial strains without promoting the development of bacterial resistance, and has regained importance in light of the growing problem of antibiotic resistance. Since 2020, several larger and high-quality studies on the efficacy and safety of methenamine for the prevention of UTIs have been published. With this study, we aim to document the routine use of Cystohipp® in clinical practice, assess disease symptoms and quality of life, and gain insights into potential influencing factors.
conditions: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

interventions.name: Female patients who suffer from recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTI) and are prescribed Cystohipp to prevent recurrence.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Documented rUTI (defined as ≥ 3 episodes in the past 12 months or ≥ 2 in the past 6 months)
•	Prophylactic measures to prevent UTIs are indicated
•	Prescription of Cystohipp® after a practical assessment of the available preventive measures
Exclusion criteria:
•	Catheterization
•	Neurogenic bladder dysfunction
•	Organic causes of increased frequency of UTIs (e.g., leading to bladder emptying dysfunction [retention, incomplete voiding])
•	Pregnancy
•	Ongoing Cystohipp® therapy
